sample_unit: model runs (10 scenarios x 3 models x 3 runs)

links.outcome: Run-to-run variability in completion of guideline-anchored safety actions for identical intraoperative crisis scenarios
links.effect: Completion varied across repeated runs in 29 of 30 model-scenario combinations; mean difference between two runs of the same model was 14.7 to 18.1 percentage points.
links.quote: The proportion of required safety actions a model completed varied across repeated runs of the same scenario in 29 of 30 model-scenario combinations.

links.outcome: Omission of communication and escalation safety actions during simulated intraoperative crises
links.effect: Omissions were highest for communication and escalation actions and varied nearly threefold across models under an identical prompt (24.6 to 72.6 percent).
links.quote: Omissions fell most on communication and escalation actions, where omission varied nearly threefold across models under an identical prompt (24.6 to 72.6 percent).

screen.reason: The study develops a guideline-anchored benchmark to evaluate the consistency and reliability of frontier LLMs during intraoperative crisis scenarios, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
